note: The declared ceiling on the E2E suite (034 FR-060, constitution v5.0.0 Principle V). A RATCHET: these numbers may only go DOWN. The build fails when a count exceeds its budget, AND when a count falls below it - because a ratchet that is never tightened is not a ratchet, it is a ceiling nobody is holding. Lower the number in the same commit that removes the tests. Raising one is a deliberate act that a reviewer will see in the diff, which is the whole point: the rule this replaces failed because growth was invisible. Before raising it, answer in one sentence what the new test can assert that a unit, component or integration test cannot.
measuredFrom: spec 034, after tagging; the migration batches lower these as they land. 041 raised @window 191→192 for one E2E: that a real shell does not swallow Ctrl+Alt+M, which no unit, component or integration test can observe because only a real ConPTY forwards keys to a shell. The total reads 560 rather than 559 because #290 raised @terminal 102→103 on master while 041 was in flight, and the two additions are independent - a rebase conflict that BOTH sides had written as 559, which is the arithmetic this ratchet exists to catch. 560->561 and @terminal 103->104 for the second half of #290, the mouse wheel: it asserts that a wheel notch still reaches a full-screen program after its panel is rebuilt, which needs a real daemon DECIDING what to replay (it withholds the tail entirely for an alt-screen program), a view genuinely torn down and rebuilt from that decision, and a real ConPTY carrying the mode sequences - no test in this repo constructs a real xterm Terminal at all, so the DEC-mode snoop and the replay do not exist on any cheaper layer. 561->562 and @terminal 104->105 for #326: that a wrapped OSC 8 hyperlink underlines on every row it occupies, with a wrapped PLAIN url as the control in the same panel - the underline is an inline style the DOM renderer writes per cell on hover, so it needs a real xterm, a real wrap and a real pointer, and the two link paths must be compared under identical width to tell which provider is at fault. 562->563, @terminal 105->106 and @window 192->193 for #199: that a window opened by a command running in a terminal ends up in the FOREGROUND rather than behind throng. The assertion is which top-level window Windows puts in front, which no lower layer has - there is no foreground to lose without a real window, a real desktop and a real process chain (throng -> daemon -> conhost -> shell -> the command -> its window), and the thing under test is precisely whether the OS honours a handoff across that chain. The policy either side of the OS call - when throng asks, and what a platform without the concept does - is pinned in packages/core/tests/unit/foreground-handoff.test.ts and deliberately NOT duplicated here. 563->565 and @window 193->195 for #382: that step-left is enabled once a reveal has moved the strip by less than one tab, and that a right-click on either step control moves nothing. The step controls render only when the strip OVERFLOWS, which is measured from laid-out widths - jsdom reports every rect as 0x0, so they never render in component/tab-strip.test.ts (its header records the decline). The arithmetic behind both is pinned in packages/core/tests/unit/tab-strip.test.ts; what is left here is the control's enabled state and which mouse button it answers. 565->568 for spec 043's User Story 5, which is the whole of what that feature spends at this layer - three tests against 51 declarations at the four cheaper layers, and the E2E line item was written into tasks.md as 'only sub-workspace syncing, real restart, and the two window chords' before any of them existed. @explorer 39->40, find-in-files-subworkspace.e2e.ts: that a Find in Files panel synced into a sub-workspace mirrors its parent's results, survives its own view being closed, and is closed when the parent panel is destroyed. Every clause is about TWO Electron windows and the relationship between them - a second BrowserWindow created by a sync, one panel id living in both, a destroy in the first that must reach the second and a close of the second that must not reach the first - and there is no window to open below this layer; subworkspace-sync.test.ts can assert what the store does when a message arrives and cannot make a window arrive. @persistence 0->1 (a NEW category entry: the tag existed in the closed vocabulary and no test carried it), find-in-files-restart.e2e.ts: that the panel a running application WROTE is the panel a second running application RESTORES, with its term, match modes, scope, replace toggle and replacement, and with no results and no pending preview. find-in-files-persistence.integration.test.ts already pins the blob round-trip and writes the row itself; what it cannot reach is the debounced save, the daemon that owns the store, the panel-type dispatch that decides what to mount and the startup restore order - four mechanisms in processes that have to be started and stopped for the question to mean anything. @window 195->196 and @core 38->39, window-chord-resolution.e2e.ts: that Ctrl+Shift+F and Ctrl+Shift+H reach the resolver through the keepShift LETTER branch. It is @core because that branch's failure mode is silence - the event is built with one modifier too many, resolves to null, and the chord is simply inert, with no throw and no log - and window-chord-manifest.test.ts's COVERED map already names both actions as pressed HERE, so an uncovered claim would be a command that can die without a test going red. The manifest guard asserts the allowlist and the branch predicate at the unit layer without pressing anything, which is precisely why the pressing half is irreducible. 568->569 and @window 196->197 for 043 T132 (FR-078, #380, US5 scenario 6), find-in-files-subworkspace.e2e.ts: that a Find in Files panel synced into a sub-workspace SHOWS the parent's results and follows them as they change. What no cheaper layer can assert is that a SECOND renderer process - its own store, its own subscription to the scan channel - ends up displaying rows it never asked for: find-in-files-snapshot.test.ts pins what one panel does with a snapshot when one arrives and file-search-viewers.integration.test.ts pins that main sends one to every viewer, but neither can make a second window exist and then ask what it is showing, which is the exact span where the defect lived. 043's figures were first written against 563, before #382 landed on master; they are restated above against master's 565. Both sides had written @window as 195 - master for #382's two tests, 043 for its own two - so a rebase conflict resolved by taking either side would have kept 195 and silently dropped two declarations. The correct merge is 197, the same arithmetic this note already records for 559.
wrappedDeclarations: The category counts come from a PER-LINE regex that wants the name and the { tag: [...] } on the SAME line as test(. A declaration wrapped across several lines - which is what a formatter does to a long one - is still counted in the total, but its tags are invisible, so it belongs to no category at all. Measured 2026-08-27: @window read 191 against a budget of 192 while the total was correct, which is a confusing failure to arrive at from the other direction. Keep the declaration on one line.
countingBasis: DECLARATIONS, not executed tests. Playwright reports a larger number for the same suite, and neither is wrong: four spec files declare tests inside a module-level loop over shell flavours, so one declaration becomes several executed tests. Declarations are what a budget should count - it is a limit on what people WRITE, and a table-driven test that gains a fifth flavour has not made the suite harder to maintain. This total also includes the @admin and @quarantine tests that grepInvert removes from a default run.
